root.name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Lasker Defense
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 d5 4. Bg5 Be7 5. e3 Ne4

overview: Black meets the pin on f6 by playing ...Ne4 (usually after ...O-O, Nf3, ...h6, Bh4), then trades off pieces: Bxe7 Qxe7 and Nxe4 dxe4 or cxd5 Nxc3 bxc3 exd5. Each exchange relieves Black's cramped position and removes the problem bishop on c8's blockers. White keeps a small space edge and usually a safe, long middlegame, with the Carlsbad-like structure or the e4 break; Black aims for ...c5 or ...Be6 development. It is a classic simplifying defence with very few risks.

white_ideas.idea: Keep the space edge and play for e4 or a central break after Rc1 and Qb3
Exchange on e7 and c3 to leave Black with a slightly passive structure
Use the open b-file and minority-attack ideas when the structure allows

black_ideas.idea: Trade pieces with ...Ne4 and ...Nxc3 to relieve the cramped position
Free the position with ...c5 or ...Be6/...Nd7 and equalise
Develop the light-squared bishop and break with ...c5

typical_structures.structure: QGD with e3/d4/c4 for White against ...d5/e6 for Black, after exchanges a Carlsbad-like structure or c3-d4 pawn chain

character.notes: Piece trades and a safe pawn structure make this very hard to break; Solid.

gambit.notes: The Queen's Gambit is not a gambit.

soundness.notes: Sound for both; a classic defence.

structure.notes: A QGD pawn centre in tension; the taxonomy treats the QGD as Flexible.

approach.notes: A main-line defence played at all levels. Standard.

level.notes: Few forced lines; Black needs to understand the exchanges and the ...c5 break. Intermediate.

sublines_that_differ.name: 9.cxd5 Nxc3 10.bxc3 exd5
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Be7 5. e3 O-O 6. Nf3 h6 7. Bh4 Ne4 8. Bxe7 Qxe7 9. cxd5 Nxc3 10. bxc3 exd5
sublines_that_differ.how: White gets a pawn majority and the bishop pair is gone, leading to a Carlsbad-like structure.

sublines_that_differ.name: 9.Nxe4 dxe4
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Be7 5. e3 O-O 6. Nf3 h6 7. Bh4 Ne4 8. Bxe7 Qxe7 9. Nxe4 dxe4
sublines_that_differ.how: Black gets a queen-side pawn lever and an advanced e4 pawn.

character.reason: Trades pieces and keeps a compact structure; very hard to lose quickly.

gambit.reason: QGD lines involve no material sacrifice.

structure.reason: The QGD centre is in tension; exchange lines can reach a Semi-open Carlsbad structure.

approach.reason: A mainstream line against the Queen's Gambit.

level.reason: Needs knowledge of the exchanges and the ...c5 break but little forcing theory.

plans.reason: The line is about simplification and no table plan is clearly characteristic.
